title: Add a JSON output option to the word count tool
summary: Users of the word count command line tool want to read its results from scripts. The tool should print the line, word and character counts as a JSON object when asked, and keep its current output otherwise.

requirements.statement: When the --json flag is given, the tool MUST print the line, word and character counts as one JSON object on standard output.
When the --json flag is not given, the tool MUST keep its current plain-text output unchanged.
When the input file cannot be read, the tool MUST write an error message to standard error and exit with a non-zero status, with or without the --json flag.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A text file with 3 lines, 7 words and 31 characters.
acceptance_scenarios.when: The user runs the tool with the --json flag and the file path.
acceptance_scenarios.then: Standard output contains one JSON object with the keys lines, words and characters set to 3, 7 and 31.

acceptance_scenarios.when: The user runs the tool with the --json flag and the file path.
acceptance_scenarios.then: Standard output contains one JSON object with all three counts set to 0.

acceptance_scenarios.given: The same text file as in the first scenario.
acceptance_scenarios.when: The user runs the tool without the --json flag.
acceptance_scenarios.then: Standard output is byte-for-byte identical to the output of the previous release.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A path that does not exist.
acceptance_scenarios.when: The user runs the tool with the --json flag and that path.
acceptance_scenarios.then: Standard output is empty, standard error explains that the file could not be read, and the exit status is not zero.

nonfunctional_requirements.statement: The tool produces JSON output for a 10 MB text file in under 2 seconds on the reference machine.

risks.description: Scripts may already parse the plain-text output, so any change to it would break them.
risks.mitigation: The plain-text output stays byte-for-byte identical and a regression test compares it with a stored sample.

open_questions.question: Should the JSON keys appear in a fixed documented order?

constraints.description: The tool must not add third-party dependencies for JSON output.

out_of_scope: Machine-readable output formats other than JSON.
Counting several files in one run.
